title: Warm pool: KV-cache priming, shard prefetch strategy, and smart eviction policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated nodes experience costly cold starts when model weights are paged in and KV caches are empty. Customers running latency-sensitive applications (QPS spikes, bursty web traffic) see p95/p99 token latency regressions during scale-up and after evictions. This ticket defines the engineering work to implement a combined warm-pool and prewarming system focused on: (1) model shard prefetch and residency scoring, (2) staged KV-cache priming (synthetic and replayed prefixes), and (3) smart eviction policies that balance memory pressure vs expected reuse. Goals: reduce cold-start p99 for reserved capacity by >= 60% for target models, keep additional cost under allocated warm-pool budget, and expose fleet controls in Console for operators and customers. This work interacts closely with autoscaler heuristics: warm nodes must be accounted for in throughput guarantees and burst capacity logic.
acceptance_criteria: Warm pool can hold N prewarmed slots per GPU type configurable via Console
Shard prefetch orders prioritized by hotness score and time-to-first-token prediction
KV priming supports two modes: synthetic-prefix replay and customer-supplied prefix bundles
Observed p99 token latency for cold scale-ups reduced by >= 60% in canary tests
Telemetry surfaces warm-pool occupancy, priming success rate, eviction events, and cost delta
Console controls to request on-demand prewarm windows and to set per-model warm budget are available behind feature flag
technical_notes: Warm-pool architecture: a short-lived pool of prewarmed containers (or processes) with model weights loaded and KV caches seeded. Separate pools for small vs large models to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Model residency scoring: combine recent-per-model QPS, last-request age, and eviction-cost estimate (weights load time + expected KV miss penalty) into a single priority value.
Shard prefetching order: prefer contiguous shard ranges to benefit IO parallelism. Use async prefetch with backpressure from GPU memory allocator.

KV priming strategies: (A) synthetic prefix generator (short prompts sampled from workload distribution) to populate prefix KV entries, (B) replay engine that replays last-K customer prefixes from request logs (configurable and opt-out for privacy), (C) customer-supplied prefix bundles via API for known warmup patterns.

Eviction policy: hybrid LRU/aging that incorporates predicted reuse score. When under memory pressure, evict shards with lowest reuse-per-cost ratio. Provide transient eviction mode during autoscale-down to avoid losing heavily primed caches.
Autoscaler integration: mark prewarmed nodes as "reserved-warm" so autoscaler treats them as capacity for throughput guarantees but with optional burstable flag to allow short reclaim windows.
Cost accounting: attribute warm pool costs to customer project or to a platform warm budget. Implement token-level cost estimation for warm-prep work to show burn rate in billing dashboard.
Privacy: any replay of customer requests must scrub PII and adhere to retention policies. Default to synthetic priming unless explicit customer opt-in. Provide audit logs for priming jobs.
Rollout toggles: feature-flag driven, start with internal canary, then invited-customer beta, then GA. Default warm pool sizes conservative for initial rollout.
Backwards compatibility: no changes to API surface for existing clients. New Console controls and a /v1/warmup API endpoint for power users and infra teams.

Test harness: use load-generator job that simulates bursty traffic and measures cold-start latency with and without warm pools; add unit tests for eviction heuristics and integration tests for KV priming correctness.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): implement core runtime priming primitives and in-memory warm pool. Feature flag off by default. Duration: 3 weeks.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 internal services. Validate p95/p99 reductions and memory stability. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for select customers via Console. Expose per-model warm budgets and prewarm windows. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (GA): enable global autoscaler accounting and billing metrics. Lift feature flag and document best-practices. Duration: 2 weeks.
Rollback plan: toggle off warm-pool flag and gracefully drain prewarmed slots. Eviction logs used to reconstruct warm-state for debugging.
